\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{صبور} (sabur)}{صبور (sabur)}]{\fa{صبور} (sabur) — patient}

\label{lesson:FA-C481-sabur}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to be proud, then the Persian for to show off.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{صبور}}
\textbf{\fa{صبور}} (\emph{sabur}) — \textquotedblleft{}patient\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{پرستار} \fa{بچه} \fa{ها} \fa{خیلی} \fa{صبور} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{parastâr-e bachchehâ kheyli sabur ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The children's nurse is very patient.
\end{quote}

An adjective. The noun is \emph{sabr} 'patience', as in \emph{sabr kardan} 'to wait'.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{sabur} was borrowed from Arabic \emph{ṣabūr}, 'patient, forbearing' (EtymDB). It belongs with \emph{sabr}, 'patience', another Arabic loan.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sabur}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sabur}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{sabur}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to be proud, then the Persian for to show off, then say \emph{sabur} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{بیصبر} (bisabr)}{بیصبر (bisabr)}]{\fa{بیصبر} (bisabr) — impatient}

\label{lesson:FA-C481-bisabr}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to show off, then the Persian for patient.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{بیصبر}}
\textbf{\fa{بیصبر}} (\emph{bisabr}) — \textquotedblleft{}impatient\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{بچه} \fa{ها} \fa{برای} \fa{باز} \fa{کردن} \fa{هدیه} \fa{ها} \fa{بیصبر} \fa{هستند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bachchehâ barâ-ye bâz kardan-e hediyehâ bisabr hastand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The children are impatient to open the presents.
\end{quote}

\emph{bi-} 'without' + \emph{sabr} 'patience'. In speech people also say \emph{howsele nadârad} 'he has no patience'.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{bisabr} is built in Persian from the prefix \emph{bi-}, 'without', and \emph{sabr}, 'patience', which was borrowed from Arabic \emph{ṣabr}: the same \emph{sabr} as in \emph{sabr kardan}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bisabr}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{bisabr}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to show off, then the Persian for patient, then say \emph{bisabr} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{تحمل} \fa{کردن} (tahammol kardan)}{تحمل کردن (tahammol kardan)}]{\fa{تحمل} \fa{کردن} (tahammol kardan) — to put up with; to bear}

\label{lesson:FA-C481-tahammol-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for patient, then the Persian for impatient.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{تحمل} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{تحمل} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{tahammol kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to put up with; to bear\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{صدای} \fa{بلند} \fa{را} \fa{تحمل} \fa{نمیکند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{u sedâ-ye boland râ tahammol nemikonad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
She can't stand loud noise.
\end{quote}

\emph{tahammol} 'endurance' + \emph{kardan}; present stem \emph{kon-}. The thing you bear takes \emph{râ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{tahammol} is a loan, usually traced to Arabic \emph{taḥammul}, 'bearing, endurance'; EtymDB has no entry for it. \emph{kardan}, 'to do', is inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{خونسرد} (khunsard)}{خونسرد (khunsard)}]{\fa{خونسرد} (khunsard) — calm, cool-headed}

\label{lesson:FA-C481-khunsard}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for impatient, then the Persian for to put up with.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{خونسرد}}
\textbf{\fa{خونسرد}} (\emph{khunsard}) — \textquotedblleft{}calm, cool-headed\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{پدرم} \fa{در} \fa{تصادف} \fa{هم} \fa{خونسرد} \fa{ماند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{pedaram dar tasâdof ham khunsard mând.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My father stayed calm even in the accident.
\end{quote}

\emph{khun} 'blood' + \emph{sard} 'cold'. Unlike English cold-blooded, it is praise: someone who keeps a cool head.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{khunsard} is built on two inherited words: \emph{khun}, 'blood', which EtymDB traces to Middle Persian \emph{xūn}, and \emph{sard}, 'cold', which it traces to Middle Persian as well (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{khunsard}, once more

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{عصبانی} \fa{شدن} ('asabâni shodan)}{عصبانی شدن ('asabâni shodan)}]{\fa{عصبانی} \fa{شدن} ('asabâni shodan) — to get angry}

\label{lesson:FA-C481-asabani-shodan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to put up with, then the Persian for calm.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{عصبانی} \fa{شدن}}
\textbf{\fa{عصبانی} \fa{شدن}} (\emph{'asabâni shodan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to get angry\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{وقتی} \fa{دیر} \fa{میرسم،} \fa{مدیرم} \fa{عصبانی} \fa{میشود}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{vaqti dir miresam, modiram 'asabâni mishavad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
When I arrive late, my boss gets angry.
\end{quote}

\emph{'asabâni} 'angry, nervous' + \emph{shodan} 'to become'; present stem \emph{shav-}. In speech: \emph{'asabâni mishe}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{'asabâni} is built in Persian on \emph{'asab}, 'nerve', a word usually traced to Arabic \emph{ʿaṣab}, with the adjective ending \emph{-âni}: 'nervy'. \emph{shodan}, 'to become', is inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
